questions.prompt: An Uno runs analogWrite(pin, 191). What duty cycle is that, in percent? Precision 0.1.
An Uno ADC (5 V reference, 10 bit) reads 820. What voltage is that, in volts? Precision 0.005.
An ESP32 12-bit ADC (nominal 3.3 V full scale) reads 1000. What voltage is that, in volts? Precision 0.002.
questions.explanation: 1000 * 3.3 / 4096 = 0.806 V (nominal; the real ADC is non-linear).

questions.prompt: ESP32 LEDC with an 80 MHz clock at 40 kHz. Maximum duty resolution in bits?
What does the Arduino expression map(300, 0, 1023, 0, 255) return? (Integer arithmetic.)
A 32-bit millis() clock reads now = 30 after wrapping; last = 4294967290. What is the unsigned difference now - last, in ms?
Why do robust sketches write last += period instead of last = now?
options: It avoids reading millis() twice in one pass.
The period stays exact; last = now would drift.
It stops millis() from overflowing after 49 days.
It makes delay() unnecessary in setup().
questions.explanation: Advancing by a whole period keeps the long-run rate exact even when a pass is late; last = now accumulates the lateness.

questions.prompt: A button is wired between an Arduino pin and ground with pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP). What does digitalRead return while it is pressed?
options: HIGH, because pressing connects the pin to the supply.
An undefined value, because the pin floats.
It alternates between HIGH and LOW at the PWM rate.
LOW, because the switch pulls the pin to ground.
questions.explanation: The pull-up holds the pin HIGH when open; closing the switch connects it to ground: LOW (active low).

questions.prompt: An ESP32 sketch reads a sensor on GPIO25 with analogRead. It works until Wi-Fi is started, then returns garbage. Why?
options: ADC2 is shared with Wi-Fi; use an ADC1 pin.
The 12-bit ADC cannot read while the CPU is busy.
Wi-Fi raises the logic level of GPIO25 to 5 V.
analogRead needs a pull-up resistor once Wi-Fi is on.
questions.explanation: GPIO25 is an ADC2 channel; the Wi-Fi driver takes ADC2. Use an ADC1 pin (GPIO32 to 39).

questions.prompt: A loop prints a 30-byte line on every pass at 9600 baud and seems stuck at about 30 passes per second. What is the cause and the remedy?
options: The compiler is slow; turn on optimisation flags in the IDE.
millis() is blocked by Serial, so call it less often.
Printing waits for the link; print rarely at 115200.
The Uno clock halves while the Serial monitor is open.
questions.explanation: 30 bytes * 10 bits / 9600 = 31 ms per line, so the buffer fills and print waits. Print rarely and use 115200 baud.

questions.prompt: Which job is the best fit for MicroPython rather than C++ on an ESP32?
options: A 20 kHz current-sampling loop.
A Wi-Fi logger posting once a minute.
Decoding encoder edges at 50 000 per second.
A bit-banged protocol with 5 us timing.
questions.explanation: MicroPython is quick to iterate and fine for slow jobs; GC pauses and speed make it a poor fit for tight timing.

questions.prompt: On an Uno (16-bit int) the code int x = 200 * 200; runs. What value does x hold?
questions.explanation: 40000 does not fit in 16-bit signed, so it wraps to 40000 - 65536 = -25536.

questions.prompt: In a three-state hold detector (IDLE, PRESSED, HELD), the button is released after 300 ms of a 1000 ms hold time. What is the next state?
options: IDLE, and the hold LED stays off.
HELD, because the press already started.
PRESSED, until the 1000 ms is over.
HELD, but with the LED off.
questions.explanation: Released before the hold time: PRESSED goes back to IDLE and the LED never turns on.

questions.prompt: Which ESP32 pin is the safest choice for a plain LED output?
options: GPIO12
GPIO34
GPIO6
GPIO18
questions.explanation: GPIO18 is a free general-purpose pin. GPIO12 is a strapping pin, GPIO34 is input only, GPIO6 to 11 connect the flash.

questions.prompt: A sketch has loop(){ digitalWrite(13,HIGH); delay(500); digitalWrite(13,LOW); delay(500); if(digitalRead(2)==LOW) digitalWrite(12,HIGH); }. Rewrite the logic so the LED blinks and the button is checked on every pass, and state the new worst-case reaction time.
rubric: Uses a last-time variable and now - last >= 500 with last += 500 to toggle pin 13, with no delay().
Reads pin 2 on every pass of loop() (INPUT_PULLUP, pressed = LOW) and writes pin 12 immediately.
States the worst-case reaction as one loop pass (well under 1 ms) instead of up to 1000 ms.

questions.prompt: Write a test plan for a millis()-based blink task that proves it survives the 32-bit rollover and keeps its period.
rubric: Injects a simulated clock and starts it shortly before 2^32 so the wrap happens during the test.
Asserts the exact toggle times (one period apart) across the rollover, including exactly one period and one tick short.
Includes a late-pass case (a skipped tick) to show last += period keeps the long-run rate.

questions.prompt: Port a loop that reads a pot and sets an LED brightness from Arduino C++ to MicroPython on an ESP32, and list two trade-offs of the port.
rubric: Maps analogRead to ADC(Pin(n)).read_u16() with attenuation set, and analogWrite/LEDC to PWM(Pin(m), freq=...).duty_u16().
Notes the changed scale (0 to 65535) and uses ticks_ms/ticks_diff for any timing.
Names trade-offs: slower execution, GC pauses and more RAM, versus faster editing and easier libraries.
